claims.text: held = [(c, why) for c in candidates] if not promotion_allowed else held = [(c, "sealed promotion: held for an explicit owner call to daedalus.kairos.gated_writes.promote_candidates" + legacy) for c in candidates]
claims.why: The code exactly implements the two branches: when promotion_allowed is false, held is populated with governance reason; otherwise with sealed promotion reason including legacy suffix.

claims.text: if not res.ok or not res.artifact: results[i] = {**base, "status": "write_gate_failed", "reason": (res.error or f"attempt state={res.state}")}
claims.why: The branch sets status 'write_gate_failed' with the specified reason when res.ok or res.artifact is false.

claims.text: if not res.artifact_path: results[i] = {**base, "status": "gated_artifact_lost", "reason": ("candidate passed its gates but its patch bytes could not be persisted after the attempt branch was reaped: " + (res.persist_error or 'no artifact path reported'))}
claims.why: The branch sets status 'gated_artifact_lost' with the specified reason when res.artifact_path is falsy.

claims.text: else: results[i] = {**base, "status": "gated_held", "reason": held_by_task.get(task_id, "held for a human to promote (daedalus.kairos.gated_writes.promote_candidates)")}
claims.why: The fallback sets status 'gated_held' with the reason from held_by_task or the default human-promotion message.

claims.text: held_by_task = {c.result.task_id: why for c, why in held}
claims.why: The comprehension maps each candidate's task_id to its held reason as written.

claims.text: write_gates = [tasks[i].get("gate") if isinstance(tasks[i].get("gate"), Mapping) else None for i in write_idx]
claims.why: The list comprehension produces the gate Mapping or None per write_idx position exactly as specified.

observations.what: The chunk relies on external functions (_governance_verdict, _provider_receipt, gate_candidates) and external types (GatedCandidate, res fields) whose behavior is not observable here.
The result records for write_gate_failed and gated_artifact_lost do not include the held reason even when held_by_task has an entry; status is determined by gate/artifact failure first.

The 'gated_artifact_lost' reason assumes the artifact was lost after branch reaping; the code does not verify that res.artifact is non-None in that branch, but it is reached only after the earlier check for res.artifact.
No explicit handling for candidates that might be missing from write_idx alignment; assumes len(candidates) == len(write_idx).
